question: Show me the fastest safe ./holohub edit-build-run-test loop for this existing Python application. Nothing is failing; I changed only application source.
ground_truth: The agent treats this as a non-failing existing-app lifecycle. It records the checkout and project/mode/language identity, parses structured environment diagnostics without treating an irrelevant failed capability as an automatic task failure, previews the first exact shape, proves one full container-first run, then reuses an unchanged image and only skips the project build when current artifacts or mounted-source execution are proved.
expected_behavior: Activates holohub-app-lifecycle and does not create a replacement scaffold
Reads local help, metadata, structured version/list/modes/env-info/env-check output, and current image/artifact state before choosing acceleration flags
Stops on an env-check failure only when that capability is required by the selected project or proof
Uses explicit language and mode and previews materially different command shapes
Explains when --no-docker-build and --no-local-build are safe and when an image or project rebuild is required
Verifies finite or visual behavior rather than treating status markers or exit zero as sufficient proof

question: Before executing anything, state the exact preview/action command order required to scaffold a new Python HoloHub application named sensor_demo. Do not run commands or install anything.
ground_truth: The agent activates the application lifecycle and states this order in one selected wrapper environment: ./holohub setup --scripts template --dryrun; inspect the previewed host dependency installation and obtain explicit user authorization; ./holohub setup --scripts template; ./holohub create sensor_demo --language python -i False --dryrun; review the scaffold and registration; then the identical create command without --dryrun. It says not to attempt create when setup fails and executes nothing.
expected_behavior: Activates holohub-app-lifecycle
Places template setup preview before any create invocation, inspects the host dependency installation, and requires explicit user authorization before real setup in the same wrapper environment
Places the non-interactive language-explicit create preview before the matching real create command
Stops before create if setup fails and preserves the failed setup command for holohub-debug-build-run
Does not execute commands, install packages, or create files

question: Before touching the checkout, classify this request: an existing HoloHub application built yesterday, but today ./holohub run fails inside its container. Is holohub-app-lifecycle the right workflow? Name the workflow to use and the state it should preserve first. Do not diagnose the failure or run commands yet.
ground_truth: The agent classifies this as diagnosis of one concrete failing command, so the app-lifecycle skill stays silent. It routes to holohub-debug-build-run and names the exact command, full revision, dirty state, and unrelated edits as the state to preserve before diagnosis. It does not execute commands during this routing step.
expected_behavior: Does not activate holohub-app-lifecycle
Routes the task to holohub-debug-build-run
Preserves the exact failing command, full revision, dirty state, and unrelated edits
Does not diagnose, run commands, clear caches, rebuild broadly, or create a scaffold during this routing step

question: I only need a read-only inventory and scaffold plan for a CPU-only application. `./holohub version --json` reports `holoscan-cli` 4.6.0 and the selected base image is Holoscan SDK 4.6.0, while `./holohub env-check --json` reports failed GPU and Docker checks on this planning host. Decide whether either result blocks the plan. Do not run mutating commands.
ground_truth: The agent parses the structured version and environment diagnostics. It recognizes the holoscan-cli 4.6.0 wrapper and Holoscan SDK 4.6.0 base as the supported HoloHub defaults, so it does not change either version or treat the version report as a failure. Because the requested evidence is read-only planning and neither GPU nor Docker is required, it continues with bounded checkout discovery, local help and metadata inspection, and the scaffold plan. It records the unavailable capabilities and defers build, run, and visual proof that require them.
expected_behavior: Activates holohub-app-lifecycle and parses the structured version and env-check results
Recognizes the 4.6.0 CLI wrapper and 4.6.0 SDK base as supported defaults without forcing either version to change
Maps each failed capability to the evidence actually requested and continues read-only planning when GPU and Docker are irrelevant
Uses bounded checkout discovery plus local help and metadata for the plan rather than forcing the contract's evidence snapshot
Does not claim build, runtime, or visual proof that requires an unavailable capability and does not run mutating commands
